rationale:
The `{cite}` of `requirements.cli.setup_css` on `src/setup.rs#fn[is_configured]` is the right role.

- **Not a test:** `is_configured` is production code, so `{test}` does not apply.
- **Not an `{impl}` root:** `requirements.cli.setup_css` obliges `habeas setup` to do three things. It must preserve existing `output.html.additional-css` entries. It must add the stylesheet at most once. It must report an error when `additional-css` is not an array. `is_configured` does none of these. It only reads `book.toml` to see whether setup has already been done. It returns `false` if `additional-css` is not an array or does not contain the expected stylesheet path. The requirement does not state that check, and `is_configured` does not modify or validate `additional-css`. So `{impl}` does not apply.
- **`{cite}` fits:** `is_configured` relies on the behavior the requirement specifies. It expects setup to have put the Habeas stylesheet into the `additional-css` array, and it returns `false` for a non-array value. A change to where or how setup records the stylesheet would require changing this check. That makes `{cite}` appropriate.
- **No redundancy:** the item has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to `requirements.cli.setup_css`. Its two `{impl}` references are to `requirements.cli.setup_project` and `requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`, so the citation is not redundant.

text: `habeas setup` MUST preserve existing entries in `output.html.additional-css` while adding the Habeas stylesheet at most once. It MUST report an error if `additional-css` is not an array.
